chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about a person who made a will, but the executor remembered only one category from it. How should he deal with the rest? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Make the remaining categories in charity (al-birr).'
ai.seo_question: What should an executor do with the parts of a will that were forgotten or not recorded?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on ambiguous wills, this narration highlights the Imam’s pragmatic approach to estate distribution when specific bequests are lost. By directing the executor to allocate the unspecified remainder to *al-birr* (general charity or goodness), the Imam ensures the deceased’s wealth continues to generate merit, reflecting the Shia principle of preserving the intent of the testator even in the absence of precise instructions.
